citation_grounding.justification: Where citations exist they are exemplary: eight GST Act sections captured with their operative words (ss 38-285, 111-5, 69-5, 9-20, 17-5, 29-70, 19-10, 29-20, 21-5), five captured ATO pages appropriately used for administrative points ($75 threshold, entertainment examples, bad-debt overview), all claim-anchored and none irrelevant. But statutory propositions at the heart of the answer rest on unverified or secondary grounding where the legislation itself was required: ss 11-5/11-25 (the basis of both positive credits) and the taxable-supply/1-11 rule for the $2,272.73 output are cited only in prose with no source, and the bank-fee rule (s 40-5) is grounded only in the ATO page — material claims a reviewer cannot audit from the package.

summary: Substantively faultless and highly usable — every conclusion matches the reference with superior statutory depth on the exclusions, tax-invoice validity and the adjustment analysis — but the positive ITC limb (ss 11-5/11-25), the output-GST rule and s 40-5 cannot be audited from the cited material, and two 'I did not read…' admissions are process narration.
